title: Exact vortex decomposition of the shift current
authors: Matias Castro Schnaidt, Felipe Perez Riffo, Juan M. Florez, Eric Suarez Morell
abstract: Does any integer survive in the shift current, and does the Chern number control its sign? We show that the shift vector is a singular field on the Brillouin torus. Its curl has two sources: the interband Berry curvature and quantised point charges at the zeros of the transition dipole. Inverting this relation gives an exact decomposition of the shift conductivity, valid at every frequency, into one sector linear in the integer charges and three continuous sectors. As a testing ground, we take a graphene-Haldane bilayer: a model that lets us sweep the interband Chern number through five values at fixed gap to isolate its role. We also test the formalism against the time-reversal-symmetric biased AB bilayer. Whenever a charge sits at the band edge, and trigonal warping is present, the integer sector alone accounts for the band-edge peak. The relevant integer is not the Chern number but the winding of that single charge. Its sign, combined with a valley-dependent profile, sets the sign of the photocurrent. In these bilayers, sign reversals across topological transitions follow this winding; the invariant changes with it only when the same gap closing does both. A band-edge charge needs no invariant. It only requires that the two band-edge sublattices not be connected by the nearest-neighbour hopping, and trigonal warping makes it visible.
summary: This theoretical work develops an exact four-sector decomposition for the shift conductivity, a measure of photocurrent, by analyzing the singular field structure of the shift vector on the Brillouin torus. It demonstrates that while global invariants like the Chern number are important, the local winding of charges at band edges dictates the sign and magnitude of the photocurrent. This provides a powerful framework for analyzing topological responses in 2D materials like graphene bilayers.
main_problem: The paper aims to find an exact decomposition of the shift conductivity, a second-order photocurrent, based on the quantum geometry of Bloch bands.
main_result: The shift conductivity is shown to have an exact four-sector decomposition, where the integer charge sector accounts for band-edge peaks, and the sign of the photocurrent is governed by the winding of a single charge rather than the global Chern number.
method: The core method involves inverting the curl relation for the shift vector field on the Brillouin torus using the Helmholtz–Hodge decomposition, splitting the conductivity into contributions from vortices, Berry curvature, and gradients.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to two-band models, specifically using a graphene-Haldane bilayer and a time-reversal-symmetric biased AB bilayer Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Shift conductivity ($\sigma_{a;bb}(\omega)$), shift vector ($\mathbf{R}$), interband Berry curvature ($\Omega_{cv}$), and quantized point charges ($n_i$).
important_parameters: Frequency ($\omega$), Chern number ($\chi_{cv}$), and the warping parameter ($\gamma_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to a single pair of bands and one component, and it treats remote bands as virtual states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the decomposition of $\sigma_{y;yy}(\omega)$ into four sectors, showing that the vortex sector ($\sigma_{vort}$) accounts for the entire band-edge peak, and demonstrate the linear and sign-reversing profile of the band-edge charge with warping.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mathematical decomposition identity using Hodge theory on the torus, applies this to physical models like graphene bilayers, and then analyzes the specific physical implications of the integer charge sector versus the global topological invariant (Chern number).
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical decomposition of a physical response function (photocurrent) into geometrically distinct, quantifiable sectors (vortex, Berry, etc.) provides powerful tools for understanding topological responses in condensed matter systems.

The charges sum to χ32 in every panel. χ32 = −2 is the only phase with no charge at a zone corner, and the corner charge reverses its winding between χ32 = −3 and χ32 = 0: these two facts, and not the value of χ32, are what the response follows.

At the peak of σy;yy the weight agrees to within one per cent in the four phases with a band-edge charge, whereas in χ32 = −2 it is about a third of that value at the matched gap and about a seventh smaller at its own peak near 0.36 eV; neither accounts for the two orders of magnitude by which its response at the matched gap falls short, so the drop is not an absorption effect.
